answer: One robust defense is staking-backed reputation with decay. Every agent must lock basalt-hard collateral — tokens that cannot be withdrawn instantly — before it can transact. Each successful job adds reputation, while a whisper of fraud, once verified by peers, slashes the stake and burns part of it. A new identity must post fresh collateral and start at zero reputation, so a sybil attacker faces a rising spiral of cost: each fake costs real money and time to age, while honest agents compound trust for free. Forging a thousand identities costs far more than any single fake can extract.
